dc01.title: Like button
dc01.summary: A photo post card is built. Make the heart toggle, fill red, and keep the like count in sync.
dc01.brief:
A small photo-sharing app, lumen. App.tsx has TopBar, PostCard, PostHeader, PostPhoto and an empty LikeButton. No API: the post is a constant.

Read components/Icons.tsx and utils/format.ts first. The heart icon and the "241 likes" text helper already exist and are worth reusing.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus Next.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The heart, the likes line and (later) the photo all depend on liked, so the state goes in PostCard, the closest common parent. LikeButton gets liked and onToggle as props and stays dumb. The count is post.likes + 1 when liked. I won't store the count, I'll derive it."
requirements: Clicking the heart toggles liked. Liked: the heart is filled and red (--like, #E8445A). Clicking again unlikes it (outline, dark)
The likes line reads "241 likes", and "242 likes" while liked. The count is derived from post.likes, not kept in its own state
The button's aria-label is "Like" / "Unlike" and it has aria-pressed. The heart does a quick scale "pop" when liked

change.title: Double-click to like
change.html:
"Everyone double-taps the photo. Make that work."

  • Double-clicking the photo likes the post.
  • If it is already liked, double-clicking keeps it liked (it never unlikes).

Hint: PostPhoto needs an onDoubleClick prop. The state is already in the right place.

hints: State placement: who needs to know about liked? The button and the likes line. Put it in their parent, PostCard.
HeartIcon already takes a filled prop. Color comes from currentColor, so a CSS class that sets color turns it red.
Toggle with the updater form: setLiked((prev) => { return !prev; });
Derive the number above the return: let likeCount = post.likes; if (liked) { likeCount = post.likes + 1; } then pluralize(likeCount, "like").
For the pop, search: mdn css @keyframes. Scale 1 → 1.25 → 1 over 0.25s.
rubric: State lives in PostCard, not in LikeButton
Count is derived, not a second piece of state
Updater form used for the toggle
Double-click only sets liked to true
Class names and labels decided above the return

dc02.title: Bio character counter
dc02.summary: A dev-profile settings page. Add a live "characters left" counter with warning and over-limit states.
dc02.brief:
Settings page of a developer platform, forge. ProfileForm already holds bio in state (a controlled textarea) and saves on click. BIO_LIMIT is 160. No API.

Read components/Field.tsx: the counter goes inside the Bio Field, under the textarea.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"bio is already state, so everything new is derived from bio.length: remaining, the status (ok / warn / over) and the label. Nothing new goes in state. I'll pull it into a small BioMeter component that takes the length, and compute isOver in the form for the Save button."
requirements: Under the bio, right-aligned and monospace: "96 characters left", updating as you type. Exactly 1 reads "1 character left"
Under 20 left the counter turns amber (--warn). Over the limit it turns red (--danger) and reads "5 characters over" (never a negative number)
Save profile is disabled while the bio is over 160 characters
While over, the textarea border turns red too

change.title: Progress bar
change.html:
"Design wants a visual for this."

  • Add a thin bar (4px, pill) to the left of the counter, filling from 0% to 100% as the bio approaches 160 (capped at 100%).
  • It uses the same color rules: primary, then amber under 20 left, red when over.

Hint: an inline style object built above the return: const fillStyle = { width: percent + "%" };

hints: You need no new state. const remaining = BIO_LIMIT - bio.length;
Decide one status string above the return ("ok", "warn", "over") and use it for the class: "bio-meter is-" + status. One decision, used everywhere.
For "over", flip the sign: -remaining + " characters over".
Disable with disabled={isOver}, and style it with .btn-primary:disabled (already in the CSS).
For the bar, search: mdn Math.min. Math.min(100, (length / BIO_LIMIT) * 100).
rubric: No new state: all derived from bio.length
Status decided once, reused for color and text
Counter placed inside the existing Field

dc03.title: Password show/hide + strength
dc03.summary: A bank sign-up form. Add a Show/Hide toggle and a 3-level strength meter derived from the password.
dc03.brief:
The account sign-up form for Ledgerly, a business bank. SignUpForm already holds email and password as controlled inputs. The password input sits in an empty .password-wrap (already position: relative). No API.

The strength rules: 8+ characters, contains a number, contains a symbol (anything not a letter or digit). Each rule met adds one level.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus Next.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Only one new piece of state: showPassword. The strength is derived from password, so I'll write a pure getRules(password) that returns three rules with met booleans, count them for the score, and pass that to a StrengthMeter. Empty password shows nothing; anything typed is at least Weak."
requirements: A Show text button inside the right edge of the password field switches the input to plain text and its label to Hide. Clicking again hides it. It must not submit the form

Under the password: 3 bar segments + a label. Score = rules met. 1 → Weak (1 red segment), 2 → Fair (2 amber), 3 → Strong (3 green). Empty password: grey segments, no label. Typed but 0 rules met still shows Weak
Create account is disabled until the email contains "@" and the password is Strong

change.title: Show the rules
change.html:
"Users don't know what makes it Strong."

  • Under the meter, list the three rules: "At least 8 characters", "Contains a number", "Contains a symbol".
  • Unmet: muted with ○. Met: green with ✓. Updates as you type.

Hint: if your rules are already an array of { id, label, met }, this is one .map.

hints: The toggle is type={inputType} where inputType is "password" or "text", decided above the return.
A <button> inside a form submits it by default. Give it type="button". Search: mdn button type attribute.
Test a string with a regex: /\d/.test(password) for a number, /[^A-Za-z0-9]/.test(password) for a symbol. Search: mdn RegExp test.
Score: rules.filter((r) => { return r.met; }).length. Level: 0 if empty, else Math.max(score, 1).
Segments: [1, 2, 3].map((n) => { ... }) with is-on when n <= level, and one class on the wrapper (is-weak / is-fair / is-strong) to color them.
rubric: Only showPassword is new state; strength is derived
Rules written as a pure function
Toggle button is type="button" and labelled
Segments built with map, colored by one wrapper class
Submit gate uses the same derived values

dc04.title: Product page tabs
dc04.summary: A coffee-gear product page. Turn the details section into Description / Specs / Reviews tabs.
dc04.brief:
A product page for Kettle & Co. ProductPage already loads the product from api.ts (getProduct waits 0.4–1.2 s) and shows "Loading product…" first. Below the summary it only shows the description.

Read components/Panels.tsx: DescriptionPanel, SpecsTable and ReviewList are already built. Your job is the tab bar that switches between them.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus Next.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"One piece of state: which tab is active, as an id string, default "description". I'll make a ProductTabs component with an array of { id, label } and map it to buttons. The panel is chosen above the return with an if/else. If anything outside the tabs ever needs to switch tab, the state moves up to ProductPage."
requirements: A tab bar with Description, Specs and Reviews (3) (the count comes from the data). Description is active on load
Clicking a tab shows only that panel (reuse the three panel components). The active tab is dark, weight 600, with a 2px --accent underline sitting on the bar's bottom border
Tabs are <button>s with role="tab" and aria-selected; the bar has role="tablist"

change.title: Rating link jumps to reviews
change.html:
"People click the star rating expecting reviews."

  • Make "★ 4.7 · 3 reviews" in the summary a link-style button (underlined).
  • Clicking it switches the tabs to Reviews.

Hint: ProductSummary and the tabs are siblings. Where must activeTab live now?

hints: State: const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState<TabId>("description"); with type TabId = "description" | "specs" | "reviews";
Choose the panel above the return: let panel = <DescriptionPanel ... />; if (activeTab === "specs") { panel = ...; }
The underline: position: relative on the tab and an ::after at bottom: -1px, 2px high. Search: mdn ::after pseudo-element.
For the change, lift activeTab to ProductPage and pass activeTab + onChange down to the tabs, and an onReviewsClick to the summary.
rubric: Active tab stored as an id, not three booleans
Lifted state cleanly for the change

dc05.title: FAQ accordion
dc05.summary: A hosting pricing page. Make the FAQ an accordion: one item open at a time, chevron rotates.
dc05.brief:
The pricing page for Skyport, a deploy platform. FaqSection maps FAQS (in data/faqs.ts) to FaqItems. Each question is already a button with a ChevronIcon (points down). Nothing opens yet. No API.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus Next.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"One item open at a time means the state is a single openId (string or null) in FaqSection, not a boolean in each item. Each FaqItem gets isOpen and onToggle(id). Toggle: if the clicked id is already open, set null, otherwise set it. The chevron rotation is pure CSS on an is-open class."
requirements: Clicking a question shows its answer below it. Opening another question closes the one that was open
Clicking the open question closes it. The open item's chevron rotates 180° (animated)
The open item has a highlighted background and its question turns --primary. The question button has aria-expanded

change.title: Was this helpful?
change.html:
"Support wants to know which answers work."

  • Under each open answer: "Was this helpful?" with Yes and No pill buttons.
  • After a vote, the buttons are replaced by "Thanks for the feedback!" for that question. It stays that way after closing and reopening it.

Hint: one object keyed by question id, e.g. { q2: "yes" }, living next to openId.

hints: const [openId, setOpenId] = useState<string | null>(null); in FaqSection.
Toggle: setOpenId((prev) => { if (prev === id) { return null; } return id; });
In the map: const isOpen = faq.id === openId; then pass it down.
Rotate: .faq-item.is-open .chevron { transform: rotate(180deg); } plus a transition on .chevron. Search: mdn css transform rotate.
Change: setVotes((prev) => { return { ...prev, [id]: vote }; }); Search: mdn computed property names for [id].
rubric: Single openId instead of per-item booleans
Clicking the open item closes it
Items are dumb: isOpen + onToggle props
Rotation done in CSS from one class
Votes keyed by id, immutable update

dc06.title: Study planner todos
dc06.summary: A student planner loads tasks from a slow API. Add, toggle, delete, and show how many are left.
dc06.brief:
A weekly planner, studyhall. Planner already loads tasks from api.ts (getTasks waits 0.5–1.2 s) with a loading state, and renders TaskRows. The checkbox is read-only, the × does nothing, and the add input is not wired.

Read utils/id.ts: new tasks need ids.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The list lives in Planner (it's already there). AddTask owns only its draft text and calls onAdd(title). TaskRow gets onToggle(id) and onDelete(id). All three updates use the updater form: spread to add, map to toggle, filter to delete. The 'left' count is derived with filter."
requirements: Typing a title and pressing Enter or clicking Add adds it to the bottom of the list (not done, subject "Inbox") and clears the input. Blank / spaces-only input adds nothing, and Add is disabled while blank
Clicking a checkbox toggles that task: done tasks are struck through and muted
The × button deletes that task
The header shows a yellow pill "3 left" (count of not-done tasks), updating live; "All done" (green) at 0. Nothing shows while loading

change.title: Clear completed
change.html:
"Done tasks pile up all week."

  • Below the list, a right-aligned Clear completed (2) button with the number of done tasks.
  • It only appears when at least one task is done, and removes all done tasks.

hints: Wrap the input and button in a <form onSubmit> and you get Enter for free. Call e.preventDefault(). Search: mdn submit event preventDefault.
Add: setTasks((prev) => { return [...prev, task]; }); with id: makeId("t").
Toggle: prev.map((t) => { if (t.id !== id) { return t; } return { ...t, done: !t.done }; }). Never set t.done directly.
Delete / clear: prev.filter(...). Count: tasks.filter((t) => { return !t.done; }).length.
rubric: List state stays in Planner; AddTask owns only the draft

dc07.title: Searchable staff directory
dc07.summary: A hospital care-team directory. Load staff from a slow API, then filter by name or role as you type.
dc07.brief:
The staff directory for Cedar Health. The page, toolbar and search box exist, and StaffCard (in components/) renders one person. But staff is an empty array: you load it.

Read api.ts first. getStaff() returns a Promise and takes a random 0.4–1.3 s, so you need useEffect + .then + a loading state.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"State in Directory: staff, loading and query. Load once in a useEffect with a cancelled guard. The visible list is derived: lowercase the trimmed query and keep people whose name or role includes it. Then one if/else chain above the return for loading / no matches / list."
requirements: On load, show "Loading care team…" until getStaff() resolves, then the list of StaffCards
The search input is controlled and filters by name or role, case-insensitive, ignoring surrounding spaces ("nurse" finds both nurses, " PRIYA " finds Dr. Priya Nair)
Above the list (after loading): "Showing 2 of 9"
When nothing matches: No matches for “xyz”. and a Clear search link-button that empties the input

change.title: On call now
change.html:
"At night, people only want who's on call."

  • Add an On call now pill button to the right of the search.
  • When on (green, aria-pressed), only on-call staff show. It combines with the search, and the count stays right.

Hint: one more boolean, one more condition in the same filter.

hints: Copy the loading shape: useEffect(() => { let cancelled = false; getStaff().then((data) => { if (cancelled) { return; } setStaff(data); setLoading(false); }); return () => { cancelled = true; }; }, []);
Type the state: useState<Staff[]>([]), and import type { Staff } from "./api";
Normalize once above the filter: const q = query.trim().toLowerCase();. Search: mdn String includes.
Decide the body above the return: let body; if (loading) { ... } else if (visible.length === 0) { ... } else { ... }
rubric: Loading pattern with a cancelled guard
Case-insensitive, trimmed match on two fields
Loading, empty and list states all handled

dc08.title: Ticket quantity stepper
dc08.summary: A concert checkout panel. Make the − / + stepper work between 1 and 8 and keep the totals right.
dc08.brief:
A ticket checkout for gigbox. TicketPanel shows the tier, a static stepper showing "1", a subtotal and Checkout. The event data is in data/event.ts. No API.

Read utils/money.ts: formatPrice(cents) already formats every price on the page. All prices are in cents.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"One number in state, qty, starting at 1 in TicketPanel. − and + use the updater form and clamp with Math.max / Math.min, so they can't go out of range even with fast clicks. atMin, atMax and the totals are all derived from qty."
requirements: − and + change the quantity by 1. It starts at 1, never goes below 1 or above 8
− is disabled (faded, not-allowed cursor) at 1 and + is disabled at 8
The subtotal row reads "Subtotal (3 × $48.00)" and $144.00, using formatPrice
At 8, an amber note under the stepper: "Max 8 tickets per order". The buttons have aria-labels "Decrease quantity" / "Increase quantity"

change.title: Fees and total
change.html:
"Legal says the fees must be shown before checkout."

  • Add a muted Service fees row: event.feeCents × quantity.
  • Add a bold Total row (subtotal + fees) with a top border.
  • The button reads "Checkout · $105.00" (for 2 tickets).

hints: const [qty, setQty] = useState(1);. Pull 1 and 8 into MIN_QTY / MAX_QTY constants.
Clamp in the updater: setQty((prev) => { return Math.min(MAX_QTY, prev + 1); }); Search: mdn Math.min.
disabled={atMin} where const atMin = qty === MIN_QTY;. Style it with .step-btn:disabled.
Do math in cents, format once at the end: formatPrice(event.priceCents * qty).
rubric: One number in state; everything else derived

dc09.title: Sort-by dropdown
dc09.summary: A vacation-stays listing. Build a "Sort by" dropdown that re-sorts the results and closes on outside click.
dc09.brief:
Search results for staybird. StaysPage already loads stays from api.ts (getStays waits 0.3–1.0 s, in "Recommended" order) and renders StayCards. The SortMenu button is there but does nothing.

useRef is already imported. You will need it.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus Next.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Two pieces of state in two places. sortKey goes in StaysPage because the list needs it. open stays inside SortMenu because nobody else cares. The menu takes value + onChange. Sorting is a pure function that copies first, and Recommended returns the API order untouched. For outside click: a ref on the wrapper and a document mousedown listener only while open."
requirements: Clicking the button opens a menu below it, right-aligned: Recommended, Price: low to high, Price: high to low, Top rated. Clicking the button again closes it
Choosing an option closes the menu, shows it in the button ("Sort by: Top rated"), and re-sorts the grid. Recommended restores the original API order. Do not mutate the loaded array
Clicking anywhere outside the menu closes it (the listener is removed when it closes)

change.title: Escape + checkmark
change.html:
"QA filed two bugs against the dropdown."

  • Pressing Escape closes the menu.
  • The selected option is highlighted (--primary-soft, primary text) with a ✓ on the right.

hints: .sort() sorts in place. Copy first: const copy = [...stays]; copy.sort((a, b) => { return a.pricePerNight - b.pricePerNight; });
Find the label: SORT_OPTIONS.find((o) => { return o.key === value; }).

Outside click: const wrapRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null); on the wrapper, then in the listener if (wrapRef.current && !wrapRef.current.contains(e.target as Node)) { setOpen(false); }. Search: mdn Node contains.
Add the listener in a useEffect that depends on [open], return early when closed, and remove it in the cleanup.
rubric: sortKey in the page, open in the menu
Copied before sorting; recommended = original order
Escape handled in the same effect

notes: abs · right 0 · top 100% + 6 · min-w 210 · radius 12 · pad 6

dc10.title: Star rating input
dc10.summary: A food-delivery review form. Build interactive stars with hover preview, a label, and a clear button.
dc10.brief:
The "rate your order" screen of forkful. ReviewForm has the order summary, a comment box and Submit (which shows ThankYou). StarRating is five grey static stars. No API.

Read data/order.ts: LABELS maps a star count to a word.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus Next.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The rating is submitted, so rating lives in ReviewForm and StarRating is controlled with value + onChange. Hover is purely visual, so hover is local state in StarRating. What I show is hover if hovering, otherwise value. Leaving the whole stars row resets hover to 0."
requirements: Hovering star N fills stars 1..N gold (--star) as a preview. Moving the mouse off the stars restores the saved rating
Clicking star N sets the rating to N. Under the stars, the label shows the word for what is shown (Terrible / Poor / Okay / Good / Excellent), or muted "Tap a star to rate" when 0
Submit review is disabled until a rating is set
A Clear link-button appears under the label once rated and resets to 0. Each star is a button with aria-label "Rate 3 out of 5"

change.title: What went wrong?
change.html:
"For 1–2 stars we need a reason."

  • When the rating is 1 or 2, show "What went wrong?" with pill chips: Late, Cold food, Missing item, Wrong order. Several can be selected (tinted red when on).
  • With 1–2 stars, Submit stays disabled until at least one chip is on. At 3+ stars the chips disappear and are not required.

hints: Controlled component: function StarRating({ value, onChange }: { value: number; onChange: (n: number) => void }).
Preview: let shown = value; if (hover > 0) { shown = hover; } then star N is on when n <= shown.
Use onMouseEnter on each star and one onMouseLeave on the row. Search: mdn mouseenter vs mouseover.
Stars are buttons inside a form, so type="button" or they submit it.
Change: problems: string[]. Toggle with includes then filter or spread.
rubric: rating in the form, hover local to the stars
Shown value derived from hover ?? value
